articles.title_orig: Fed Chair Warsh says central bank to reduce the number of rate-setting meetings in coming years
articles.title_zh: Fed Chair Warsh says central bank to reduce the number of rate-setting meetings in coming years
articles.content_orig:
The Federal Reserve held steady on rates at the conclusion of its October meeting, maintaining its target range of 3.75% to 4%.
Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented from the decision: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack were in favor of raising rates by a quarter percentage point.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced that the central bank will reduce he number of rate-setting meetings starting in 2027, noting that while eight meetings per year is "the right number" for the FOMC, one of them will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy starting in 2027. The remainder will be policy-setting meetings.
In 2028, the Fed will plan to host two meetings focused on strategy discussions and the remaining six will be centered on policy setting, Warsh said.
At these policy meetings that will specifically focus on broad strategy, Warsh said he doesn't anticipate that the Fed will make a rate decision or release a statement.
He then said "it's not obvious yet" what the Fed would share following these meetings.
"There's more news to come on that," Warsh said. "The decision on the new format for the meetings is relatively new."
Warsh said there was a "robust discussion" on how to handle these meetings over a few gatherings.
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said economic growth has been positive after the agency maintained rates at its October meeting, keeping rates at a range between 3.75% and 4%.
"Economic growth has strengthened. The GDP increase in the first half of this year was revised up from an earlier estimate of 1.8 percent up to 2.4 percent, and the third quarter appears to have brought an even more rapid advance," Warsh said.
Warsh said the Fed's discussion over recent days "focused mainly on the price stability side of our remit."
He said the full employment side of its dual mandate has been "quite positive," citing a decreasing jobless rate compared with a year ago. Warsh also noted that the unemployment insurance claims volume, when looking at a four-week average, is at "the lowest level in generations."
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said the central bank will cut back on the number of meetings where members vote on rates. Said Warsh: "We believe eight meetings per year is the right number for the FOMC, but in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated. The rest will be regular FOMC policy setting meetings, and I expect that in 2028 we'll have two meetings dedicated discussions of strategy and six for setting policy."
Later Warsh added that he doesn't "anticipate" making a policy decision during these strategy meetings.
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said that following the decision by the central bank to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at its September meeting, there are signs that financial conditions have tightened since.
"We have started to see some changes in financial and credit conditions; they have tightened for some businesses and households, much as we would expect," he said. "Market participants are becoming somewhat more discerning in their capital allocations."
He added, though, that he wouldn't call financial conditions broadly "tight," but rather they are helping create a path toward price stability.
An unusual dissent from a Fed Governor on the rate decision could stem from anger over the legal actions of President Donald Trump's administration', according to Chris Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS.
Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook was one of two dissenters on Wednesday's decision to keep rates unchanged. Cook has battled the White House in court after Trump attempted to fire her. Trump has cited mortgage fraud, allegations that she has denied.
It's "very rare to see a Fed governor dissent, they are sitting right there in the same building as the Chairman," Rupkey said. "This could have been a protest vote as the Trump administration is taking steps to get Fed governor Cook to resign one way or another."
The Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady at the October meeting suggests the central bank's prior hawkish stance was a matter of empty showmanship, according to Cem Karsan, founder and CIO at Kai Wealth.
"This, in my opinion, is kabuki theater," Karsan told CNBC's "Power Lunch" on Wednesday. "At the end of the day, they're trying to gain credibility. Keep the Fed independent for now, ultimately, in terms of what they're saying. But ultimately, the only way to respond to what's important, which is the long end of the curve, is through more dovishness from the Fed, which will be coming in the months and quarters to come. I believe that is the next move."
"This is a matter of credibility. This is a matter of trying to state that they are being thoughtful of inflation," he continued. "But at the end of the day, nothing has changed going into Jackson Hole, and nothing has changed coming out."
In its post-meeting statement, the Fed indicated it will need more data to guide its next steps on policy.
"Inflation remains elevated," central bank policymakers said in the statement.
"The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability."
Read more from CNBC's Alex Harring on what's changed in the Fed's statement .
Central bank policymakers opted to hold rates at their current target range of 3.75% to 4%, a move that traders largely expected.
Two members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissented from the decision: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack were in favor of raising rates by a quarter percentage point.
Read more from CNBC's Jeff Cox on the Fed's decision .
The three major averages were mixed as the Federal Reserve's rate decision approached.
As of 1:40 p.m. ET, the S&P 500 was up 0.2%, while the Dow Industrials gained 135 points, or 0.3%, on the day. The Nasdaq Composite traded near the flatline.
The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was up more than 2 basis points at 5.02%, while the 2-year yield gained almost 3 basis points to 4.766%.
If the Fed waits until December to lift rates, it would "just be prolonging our agony," said Steven Wieting, co-founder of the CIO Group.
Fed funds futures traders are largely expecting the central bank to keep rates unchanged on Wednesday and then raise them in December. Traders are placing just around 7% likelihood of a 25 basis point hike on Wednesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
But Wieting told CNBC on Wednesday that there's a chance that central bank policymakers may not hold off after Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has signaled that inflation remains too high. He said raising rates now "may be better" than not doing so until December.
"I'm not predicting action today," Wieting said. "But the chance that they actually shock us now is above 7%."
While the Federal Reserve is largely expected to stand pat on its key interest rate on Wednesday, consumer rates have edged higher since policymakers pushed through their first hike last month.
The average 30-year fixed rate mortgage now sits at 7.33%, up from 7.12% last month, according to MND. Mortgage rates are closely tied to movement in the 10-year Treasury yield, which is now just below 5%.
The cost of borrowing against the equity in your dwelling – a home equity loan – has also risen and is now at 8.77%, versus 8.28% in September, according to Bankrate.
Savers have seen some marginal gains in the past month since the Fed lifted its rate by a quarter percentage point in September. The average money market annual yield is now at 0.45%, up one basis point from last month, according to Haver. The annual percentage yield on a five-year certificate of deposit is at 1.83%, up eight basis points from September, per Haver.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.content_orig:
Qatari mediators on Sunday handed Iran a new draft deal to end the war, the Reuters news agency reported, citing an official briefed on the negotiations.
Tehran is considering the proposal and set to respond by the end of the week, the agency reported Wednesday.
The source added that there were concerns in Tehran before the meeting on Sunday that Israel could resume its bombardment of Iran this week.
The cost of the Iran war has risen to an estimated $47 billion, according to an estimate from the U.S. military's Central Command obtained by CBS News Tuesday.
Like previous estimates, it does not include damage to U.S. military bases in the Middle East. The bulk of the cost, $29 billion, is for replacing expended munitions.
According to a report released by the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office in September, the Iran war could cost approximately $2 billion to $3 billion per month for as long as it continues.
Exit polls from Israel's major television networks project that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition in Tuesday's election, but his Likud party still emerged as the largest party among all the contenders. Neither bloc, Netanyahu or the opposition, has a clear majority.
While Netanyahu appears to have won fewer votes than his main challenger, according to the early exit polls, both candidates will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.
One or the other would need to obtain majority support in Israel's 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, in order to form a government.
Israel's two Arab parties won more seats in parliament than in any previous election. That electoral success comes after what some Arab voters told CBS News was a difficult time for them in the country under the hard-right government of Netanyahu, prompting a historic turnout for the minority community.
Both Netanyahu and those opposing him have vowed not to form a government reliant on Arab parties, arguing it would endanger the country if they gain enough seats to influence Israel's engagement in its myriad conflicts. Arab citizens of Israel are around 20% of the population.

articles.title_orig: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.title_zh: Spain train crash kills at least 68 as witnesses describe devastating scenes
articles.content_orig:
Aerial footage showed the aftermath of a deadly high-speed train crash in central Spain Wednesday. (Spanish Civil Guard via AP)
Several Americans are believed to have been injured in a high-speed train collision that killed at least 68 people in Spain on Wednesday when one train collided with another that had stopped on the tracks.
The crash took place in Spain's Castilla-La Mancha, with the regional government confirming the death toll and adding that another 58 people required medical treatment in hospitals. Several Americans are believed to have been hurt in the crash, according to the State Department.
Rescue workers continue to search in the wreckage for survivors and bodies, with witnesses describing a gruesome scene.
Wednesday's incident is the second high-speed rail crash Spain has suffered this year. Esther Padilla, spokeswoman for the regional government, said the cause of the crash is not yet known.
Spain’s rail system operator ADIF said the crash occurred Wednesday morning in the province of Toledo. Both trains were carrying hundreds of passengers, and were headed in the same direction on a route from Madrid to Seville.
CRASH INVOLVING SPEEDING TRAIN, MINIBUS IN BELGIUM LEAVES 4 DEAD INCLUDING 2 CHILDREN
Emergency services attend to victims at the scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Juanma Jiménez/Europa Press via AP)
One train, run by the state-owned RENFE company, ran into the tail of the other train owned by private company IRYO that had stopped, knocking two of its cars off the track. Those companies were the same ones involved in January's crash.
Padilla said 397 passengers were on the RENFE train and 147 passengers on the IRYO train.
David Gómez, a construction worker, was working with his brother and another colleague nearby when they heard the crash and ran to help, he told the newspaper El País.
"People were trying to get out through the windows…. We cut through some fences to access the area and treated people with the first-aid kits we had brought," until emergency services arrived, he said. "As I was trying to pull a young woman out, there was a piece of a leg."
Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said emergency workers were focusing on rescuing survivors and bodies from the two most damaged train cars. She said the injured are being sent to different hospitals in the area.
BYSTANDER VIDEO CAPTURES NORFOLK SOUTHERN TRAIN T-BONING SEPTIC TRUCK AT VIRGINIA RAILROAD CROSSING
The scene of a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Juanma Jiménez/Europa Press via AP)
"It was a high-speed impact, so we are expecting this to be a tragedy," García said.
Passenger Ignacio Relaño was traveling on the RENFE train. He told state broadcaster TVE that the train had stopped momentarily on the line before it started again and then crashed into the IRYO.
"We all felt the train abruptly slowing down and then the impact," he said. "The car leaned to one side like it was about to tip over. I hit my nose, everything went flying, luggage, cellphones. Everything shook."
Another passenger recounted to Cadena Ser radio how she felt the train slam on the brakes and was thrown forward in her seat, breaking the small table in front of her. She said she saw body parts and trapped people covered in blood.
Passengers wait at Santa Justa station in Seville, Andalusia, Spain, following a train accident near Urda, Toledo, on Oct. 28, 2026. The collision suspended services on the Madrid-Andalusia high-speed line. (Europa Press via Getty Images)
IRYO, an Italian-owned company, said in a statement that it has "activated its security protocols and is closely working with authorities."
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez canceled his agenda to focus on the crash. He wrote on X that he was "dismayed by the serious train accident in Toledo."
"Emergency services are working on site to attend to the affected passengers," wrote Sánchez, who faces a national election next month. "All my thoughts are with the victims and their families."

Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia said in a short statement on X that they were following news of the accident.
"We are deeply saddened and concerned by the train accident in Urda (Toledo)," the royal couple said. "We share in the grief of the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, and we send our heartfelt support to the injured and all those affected."

articles.title_orig: Why China is desperate to ship cars overseas
articles.title_zh: Why China is desperate to ship cars overseas
articles.content_orig:
To understand why China is desperate to ship cars overseas, visit a dealership in Beijing.
Autumn has traditionally been the peak time to buy vehicles in the country, but this year many showrooms are empty or shut.
Car salesman Li Ke said that other than the Covid-19 pandemic, the 2026 "golden September and silver October" season, as it's known, is the slowest he's seen in his 26 years on the job.
"In past years, customers would come to the showrooms nonstop," he told CNBC during an interview in his deserted showroom at a complex of dealerships on the outskirts of the Chinese capital. "We would have deals to sign every day. But nowadays we see only two to three deals a week. It's a dramatic drop."
Many people in China aren't buying cars because an unstable job market and a continued slide in property prices have undercut consumer confidence. The government has also scaled back incentives such as cash-for-clunkers subsidies and tax breaks to go electric, car salespeople said.
Passenger car retail sales for 2026 in China totaled 13.33 million units through September, falling 21.7% from a year ago, according to the China Passenger Car Association. For the full year 2026, China's domestic passenger car retail sales are set to drop 22% to 18.5 million vehicles, the association said — under the level recorded in the first year of the pandemic.
Even electric vehicles, which were once a bright spot, are down. Gasoline car sales have been declining in China because of the country's transition to electric vehicles, but sales in China of new-energy vehicles — which includes EVs — dropped by 12.8% from January through September, according to the association.
"Customers are watching every penny," Li said. "When looking at all the new functions on all these new models, they are weighing what is most practical, economic and worth their money over the long term. We don't see impulse buying. Because of the bad economy, people are taking more time to replace their cars."
The fierce competition has led to bruising price wars in recent years, a key reason Chinese carmakers have cast their eyes overseas and why Beijing is fearful of partners like the U.S. and Europe putting up coordinated trade barriers against its massive car exports, analysts said.
Industrial profits for the first nine months of the year were up 15.5% from the same period in 2025, but September showed signs of weakness relative to the prior eight months, according to China's National Bureau of Statistics . For the auto manufacturing industry specifically, profits from January to September shrank by 22.8% compared with last year.
To preserve cash, Li's dealership moved out of a pricey streetside space to one with less foot traffic but that rents at a fraction of the cost.
With profit margins eroding, Li said he sees little point in offering further discounts. He said the bigger hurdle is the prevailing Chinese consumer attitude toward big-ticket purchases.
"Chinese buyers would rather wait," he said.

articles.title_orig: Apple Unveils Touch-Screen MacBook Pro, Reversing Longheld Jobs Stance
articles.title_zh: Apple Unveils Touch-Screen MacBook Pro, Reversing Longheld Jobs Stance
articles.content_orig:
Apple on Wednesday announced its first laptop with a touch screen, which it is calling MacBook Pro with ProLED XDR Display.
Apple said that the laptop has a new display, using OLED technology, that offers more brightness, better colors and wider viewing angles. It's using Apple's M5 Pro or Max chips, and Apple said on Wednesday that it's lighter than Apple's current pro laptops.
It's still an Apple laptop, and is running MacOS, not a version of the iPhone or iPad operating system. In a video, Apple showed users swiping on the screen to manipulate videos or images. It also has a glowing Apple logo on the laptop's lid.
The new laptop will go on sale on Nov. 6 and the 14-inch version will start at $2,899. The 16-inch version will cost at least $3,399. Both are notable price increases from existing models.
This is Apple's third major product launch under new CEO John Ternus, signaling a faster cadence for hardware releases. It's also a major reversal for Apple, which has resisted putting touchscreens on its laptops for decades as some Windows machines gained the feature.
"Yes, for the very first time, we are bringing touch to the Mac," Ternus said in live remarks to media and analysts in Los Angeles.
The new MacBook Pro comes at a time when the laptop market has been going through one of its worst slumps ever. Overall shipments are expected to be down 11% this year. Analysts say the AI-driven global market shortage of memory has contributed to higher laptop prices, which has hurt sales and demand.
In the third quarter, total PC shipments dropped 20% on a year-over-year basis, according to market researcher IDC. Apple's own shipments fell 11% during the quarter, according to the estimate.
Even Apple's not immune to rising memory prices, after former CEO Tim Cook warned this summer that the situation around memory prices was "unsustainable." Nearly all Macs got price hikes this year. Mac Minis introduced in August got a $300 bump, for example.
The announcement caps a busy two months of product launches under Ternus.
Apple also introduced new iMac and MacBook Pro models with M6 chips this week, after price hikes to the lineup totaling several hundred dollars in June. Apple introduced an iPad Mini on Monday that starts at $699, $100 more than its predecessor.
In September, Apple released new iPhones, including its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo. It also revealed a new smart speaker with a display called HomeView that uses a redesigned version of Siri to answer a broader range of questions.
The launch signifies the growing strategic importance of the Mac to Apple, despite it generating less revenue than the iPhone. In the most recent quarter, Apple reported $10.35 billion in Mac sales, or just under 10% of the company's total revenue.
But many software developers swear by the Mac, and it remains the only supported platform to develop iPhone apps. And in recent months, Apple has highlighted its chips and memory architecture to make the case that its computers are the best fit for local or edge AI that runs on a device, instead of the cloud.
Meta's AI model developer team bought hundreds of Mac Minis this year to test agents, for example. And Apple notably teamed up with Meta earlier this month to make an announcement that large, nearly frontier models can run on clusters of Macs connected with high-speed cabling, allowing developers to run agentic code without paying Anthropic or OpenAI.
Apple has had a historical resistance to touchscreen laptops — software chief Craig Federighi explained in 2018 that the ergonomics would fatigue users. "We make the world's best touch computer on an iPad. It's totally optimized for that. And the Mac is totally optimized for indirect input. We haven't really felt a reason to change that," Ternus, then Apple's senior VP of hardware engineering, told The Wall Street Journal's Joanna Stern in 2021.
Ternus has been working on Macs since he joined the company and was credited along with silicon chief Johny Srouji as the leader of Apple's effort to get Macs running on Apple's chips, not Intel's. Apple credited Ternus' work on Mac in its official CEO transition statement .
That may be why Ternus in his early days as CEO will be the executive to backtrack on a long-running Apple design philosophy.
Touchscreen laptops have been available on Windows machines for a long time, but they're just another feature, not a selling point behind most purchasing decisions, Ryan Reith, IDC VP for worldwide device trackers, said.
Only 17% of notebook PCs shipped globally this year will have touchscreens, according to IDC data. Touchscreen laptops also have a slightly lower average selling price than non-touchscreen notebooks.
Hardware technology hasn't been the limiting factor for Apple merging its desktop and mobile interfaces, he added, and Apple could have been waiting to launch a touchscreen laptop until it could present a good user experience and perfect its software after attempts to make its iPad more like a laptop.
"This is really a user interface and software thing," Reith said. "It's one more thing that can draw the developers in."

The move comes just days ahead of the US midterm elections, in which the rising cost of living has been a key issue
The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.
The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 to 4.00 per cent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.
“The accumulation of more information will help the committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the committee’s 2 per cent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.

Shares of Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) popped on Wednesday, jumping as much as 5.5%. As of 11:31 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 4.8%.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist higher was a rival's robust financial report.
Image source: Getty Images.
Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) reported its fiscal 2026 third-quarter results, and investors were clearly impressed. The company reported record revenue of 104.6 trillion South Korean Won (roughly $78.9 billion), up 328% year over year and 32% quarter over quarter. At the same time, operating profit of 83.3 trillion won (roughly $61.7 billion) soared 632% year over year and 38% sequentially.
For context, analysts' consensus estimates called for revenue of 98.34 trillion won and operating profit of about 76.7 trillion won, so the results easily surpassed investor expectations.
However, what really turned heads was management commentary about the state of the industry. SK Hynix's outlook speaks volumes: "Demand [is] expected to outpace supply through 2030." The company also noted that its supply is essentially sold out for the next three years. There have been fears that demand for memory chips would begin to decline starting in 2028, so this pronouncement was cheered by investors.
The company also announced that it would return 100 trillion won to shareholders, including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won via share buybacks.
As one of the Big Three computer memory manufacturers, Micron will benefit from the ongoing demand for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM), and NAND flash memory chips -- all critical to the ongoing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI).
Despite stock price gains of more than 340% over the past year (as of this writing), Micron stock is selling for just 13 times earnings, a valuation that is all the more attractive given that the company continues to deliver revenue and profit growth in the triple digits. Moreover, SK Hynix seemed to confirm that the current demand cycle will continue for several more years, and Micron has adopted measures to lock its major customers into multi-year, non-cancelable contracts, thus ensuring the boon continues.
That's why Micron stock is still a buy.

The show featured a total of 23 games over the course of its 15-minute runtime, showing a selection of indie games coming to Switch and Switch 2 .

articles.title_orig: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position
articles.title_zh: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position
articles.content_orig:
Andy Burnham has insisted there is "no confusion" over his position on the European Union, as he criticised the UK's current deal with the bloc.
The prime minister said it was his "responsibility" to improve the deal, which was ratified in 2020, at a summit in Brussels next month.
He denied he had shifted his stance since the Makerfield by-election when he promised not to "re-run" the Brexit debate . Earlier this week, he suggested he could call a referendum on the UK returning to EU freedom of movement, before No10 appeared to backtrack .
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused him during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday of failing to "respect" the 2016 Brexit vote.
Badenoch said Burnham had created confusion and asked if he wanted a referendum on rejoining the EU.
"There is no confusion at all," Burnham told MPs.
"The government has a collectively agreed position, which I have set out today.
"It is entirely consistent with everything that I've said, including in the by-election.
"The red lines in our manifesto, including on freedom of movement, will stay in place firmly for the whole of this Parliament."
Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.
Freedom of movement allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country.
It is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market, which enables goods, services and people to move freely between EU member states.
Badenoch accused Burnham of having "opened his mouth without engaging his brain" over freedom of movement during "the chancellor's big week" as the Budget is unveiled .
Recalling the mood in Parliament and the country in 2017 when the current Brexit deal was being fought over, Badenoch said: "We do not want to go through that again - the country was paralysed.
"It was miserable, regardless of which side of the debate you were on."
Burnham said Badenoch was "speaking the truth" here and the country had suffered from low growth and insufficient control on migration as a result of a "harder Brexit than what was promised" in the 2016 referendum.
"Where I am focused is getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility, and I will lead from this despatch box over the next few weeks," Burnham said.
At a summit in Brussels on 20 November, Burnham will push options for a reset of relations with the bloc on issues such as youth mobility, food, drink, energy and cooperation on illegal immigration.
Burnham's comments at Prime Minister's Questions came as a letter emerged addressed to his Cabinet ministers, asking them to be "aligned and disciplined" around the summit.
"It will not be appropriate for ministers individually to advocate for specific options or opine on the likely outcome of the process," he wrote in a letter on Wednesday.
He said he hoped the summit led to "some important, concrete steps" and he would set out the next steps "to consider the UK's long-term relationship with the EU as part of our 10-year plan".
"Both the UK and the EU have changed considerably in the 10 years since the Brexit vote," he said.
"Any future relationship depends on practical arrangements that are realistic for both sides, and responsive to this new reality."
Any "fundamental change" to this relationship "would be for the public to decide and a matter for the next Parliament," he added.

articles.title_zh: Spain Train Crash Live Updates: At Least 68 Killed in High-Speed Train Collision, Officials Say
articles.content_orig:
Toledo, Spain 6:07 p.m. Oct. 28
A high-speed passenger train rear-ended another in Spain on Wednesday morning near the central city of Toledo, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens more, officials said, in one of the deadliest train crashes in Spanish history.
The cause of the crash, which sent parts of both trains down a rural embankment, was not immediately clear. It was the second lethal crash this year involving the same two rail operators, and it was likely to deepen doubts about the security of Spain’s once-vaunted rail system.
In Spanish news reports, passengers described an awful impact that tossed people from a dining car, broke limbs and piled passengers atop one another. People crawled out of windows and lay in a nearby field, where local workers, who had heard the crash, rushed to help them with first aid kits and saw the first bodies.
The crash also came about a month ahead of national elections, and it had the potential to become an issue in an already bitter campaign about the competence of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s left-wing government.
Sixty-eight people were seriously injured in the crash, 15 of them critically, said Emiliano García-Page, the president of the Castilla-La Mancha region.
Spain’s rail authority, the Adif, said the trains involved were a “Renfe train and another from the Iryo company,” both covering the route between Madrid, the capital, and the southern city of Seville. Renfe is the national rail provider.
Initial reports suggested that the Iryo train was stopped on the tracks, and that the Renfe train barreled into it. Local news outlets reported that there were 397 passengers aboard the Renfe train and about 150 aboard the Iryo train.
Trains from the same operators collided on a southern line in January, leaving 46 people dead.
Isaac Barrientos, a spokesman for the government’s transportation ministry, said on Wednesday that initial reports indicated two carriages of the Iryo train had derailed. He said all traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia route had been suspended until further notice.
Mr. Sánchez visited the scene of the crash on Wednesday afternoon, saying that Spanish rail’s security systems clearly needed to be reinforced. “If there has been negligence, it will come to light,” he said. “If there have been failures in the safety system, we will respond with the utmost firmness.” He declared three days of official mourning.
The conservative opposition leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, quickly voiced his own concern.
“I am very concerned about the information we are receiving regarding another train accident,” he wrote on social media soon after the crash. “The priority now is to assist the victims and support their families. My full support goes to the emergency teams working on the ground.” His Popular Party canceled all its campaign events around the country.
Another deadly crash: In January , a northbound Iryo train derailed, two of its cars falling onto the opposite track, and a southbound Renfe train slammed into the carriages seconds later. An official report on what caused that lethal accident has not been released, but preliminary investigations pointed to a broken rail as the likely cause.
A detailed account: In a news conference, Spain’s transportation minister described the events that he said preceded the crash on Wednesday.
José Bautista contributed reporting from the scene of the crash.
The U.S. State Department said in a statement that several U.S. citizens were among those injured in the crash. It did not provide information about their conditions.
Spain’s transportation minister said a train crash that killed dozens on Wednesday appeared to result from an “inexplicable” decision by traffic control operators to tell a high-speed train to continue its journey when another train was stopped farther along the tracks.
The minister, Óscar Puente, said he spent the morning watching a reconstruction of the accident and listening to audio recordings of communications between the control center in Madrid and the trains that crashed near Toledo, and he gave a detailed account of what he said preceded the crash at a news conference.
At about 8:30 a.m. local time, an automatic train control system near the site of the crash went down because of a computer failure, Mr. Puente said.
The system — known as the Linienzugbeeinflussung or LZB — dates to the 1960s and uses external technologies, such as track circuits and axel counters, to monitor the speed and position of trains. This information allows the system to automatically calculate when and how quickly a train can safely move forward. It then changes railroad signals accordingly.
On Wednesday, the safety system was inactive along a stretch of about 39 miles, or 63 kilometers, of tracks, so six trains traveling along that section were automatically stopped as a precaution. At that point, he said, the control center in Madrid took over.
“The control center communicated with the trains that had stopped, and at 8:36 a.m., the decision was made to allow the train that eventually collided with the stationary Iryo train to resume its journey as normal,” Mr. Puente said, referring to the private rail operator of the stopped train.
Traffic controllers working for Adif, the state-owned company that manages Spain’s rail infrastructure, told the train that eventually rear-ended the other to restart its planned journey, Mr. Puente said, “despite there being another train ahead of it.”
The train that was hit from behind was believed to have received instructions from traffic operators to continue, he said, but for unknown reasons it did not proceed.
The moving train then hit the stationary train.
“And that is the origin of the accident that has taken place,” Mr. Puente said, adding that the moving train should have been stopped according to protocol.
The Madrid-Seville route is currently undergoing a modernization program that will replace the LZB system with the more modern European Rail Traffic Management System. Infrastructure officials hope that the new system will cut down on human error in signaling.
Mr. Puente also said that the driver of an uninvolved train tried to warn the control center of the dangers when its operators greenlit the rear train’s resumption of its journey. That driver told the control center operator that trains should proceed at lower-than-normal speeds. The operator, Mr. Puente said, acknowledged his error. “Oh, yes,” the operator replied.
K. R. Callaway contributed reporting.
When the crash happened, Yahadi Mohamed Maulud, 41, who lives in the nearby town of Yébenes, loaded his car with water bottles and rushed to help. “We found a massacre,” he said, describing torn limbs and a blood-covered woman searching for her brother. One of the first to arrive at the scene, he helped to move injured passengers and carry stretchers. Mr. Maulud said he often took the train himself to Madrid for business, but no more: “I’m never getting on that train again.”
So many people showed up at Madrid hospitals on Wednesday to donate blood for victims of the train crash that the authorities are asking citizens to wait until Thursday or the following days, when more donations will be needed.
“The response from the people of Madrid to the call for blood donations is overwhelming,” said Isabel Díaz Ayuso, Madrid’s regional president. “Thank you, everyone.”
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez spoke from the scene of the crash on Wednesday afternoon. “It’s not possible for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed train accidents in one year,” he said, adding that while today’s accident and a fatal January crash on the same line seemed unrelated, Spanish rail’s security systems clearly needed to be reinforced.
“If there has been negligence, it will come to light,” he said. “If there have been failures in the safety system, we will respond with the utmost firmness.” Spain needs to understand “what is the origin of this tragedy,” he said.

articles.content_orig:
Study suggests the long-term fate of the solar system, including Earth, ‘may be far more complicated than predicted’, according to scientist
When a star like our sun grows old, it puffs up into a red giant that can gobble up its nearest planets.
But Chinese astronomers say they have found three solar systems where planets should have been eaten this way yet somehow survived – a puzzle that could change how scientists picture Earth’s distant future.
Using Nasa’s TESS space telescope, a team led by Qian Shengbang from Yunnan University showed that three Jupiter-like planets – each hugging an ageing star in the northern sky – had lived through their hosts ballooning out past them before shrinking back.

articles.title_orig: ‘Noah’s Ark remains’ found burned and buried 30 feet below final resting place: report
articles.title_zh: ‘Noah’s Ark remains’ found burned and buried 30 feet below final resting place: report
articles.content_orig:
They’re the real raiders of the lost Ark.
Researchers claim they’ve potentially discovered wood from Noah’s Ark in Eastern Turkey, potentially cracking a caper that has eluded believers for thousands of years.
The so-called discovery was reportedly made in the Durupınar Formation , a roughly 538-foot-long geological structure near Mount Ararat.
Discovered in 1959, site has fascinated Ark hunters for decades due to its ship shape and proximity to the events in the Bible.
In the religious text, the legendary vessel sheltered Noah, his family and Earth’s animals during an apocalyptic flood some 4,300 years ago.
After studying the repository for years, researchers feel they’ve found evidence that the site is indeed the Ark’s final resting place, dispelling theories that it formed naturally.
Andrew Jones, project head and founder of Noah’s Ark Scans, told the Daily Mail that they’ve discovered both charred and uncharred wood nearly 30 feet underground, which could potentially be “the charred remains of Noah’s Ark.”
However, Jones notes that the wood could entail the remains of a campfire a shepherd had started while sheltering inside the Ark hundreds of years ago.
Although they’re unsure if it was purposefully set alight or ignited via lightning strike or volcanic eruption.
Coincidentally, in the Bible story, Noah is told to cover the Ark in pitch, a waterproofing chemical that is also highly flammable.
According to the researchers, the blaze might’ve helped preserve the remnants by slowing the decomposition of wood in soil.
Either way, this marks the latest in a series of clues that supposedly support the boat’s biblical provenance.
Previously, Noah’s Ark Scans used ground-penetrating radar to map what they claim is a series of subterranean chambers and tunnels at the site, whose dimensions mirror those described in the bible.
These underground corridors reportedly led to a central cavity that Jones dubbed the “Atrium.”
“God told Noah to bring the animals in,” Jones told GB News in the Spring while explaining the alleged significance of the so-called quarters. “And so these animals would have stayed there, plus Noah and his family.”
Meanwhile, soil analysis revealed that the inside dirt harbored three times more organic matter  — and 38% more potassium — than samples taken right outside, hinting at its unnatural origins.
Jones said his team’s case was strengthened this past fall when a drilling and scanning expedition revealed that there was no natural bedrock beneath the formation as many critics claim.
Instead, they found rich black soil, which researchers plan to test for signs of decayed wood and other alleged signs of the Ark this winter.
“Noah’s Ark was a giant wooden boat, according to the Bible,” said Jones. “As wood decays, you’re gonna find elevated organic matter.”

Jerusalem 9:00 p.m. Oct. 28
Isabel Kershner Johnatan Reiss Aaron Boxerman Qasim Nauman and Leo Sands
Israel’s political leaders were poised for weeks of negotiations over the shape of the next government, as initial results on Wednesday showed no clear winner in a tightly fought election that many have described as a make-or-break moment for the country.
If neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hard-line alliance nor an opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot win enough seats to form a government, both would need to find support from outside their blocs for backing as prime minister.
By Wednesday evening, election officials had counted about 80 percent of ballots. Those votes, alongside exit polls, indicate that neither bloc would reach the 61 seats needed to secure a straightforward majority in the Knesset, Israel’s Parliament.
Some of Mr. Netanyahu’s allies are floating the idea that he could join Mr. Eisenkot and other centrists to form a broad unity government to stay in power. For Mr. Netanyahu, the long-serving prime minister who remains as a caretaker until a government is formed, that would be a comfortable scenario, as long as he remained on top.
His primary rival, Mr. Eisenkot, faces a dilemma of his own: He has denounced Mr. Netanyahu as unfit to lead Israel, but he has also objected to partnering with Arab parties in a potential coalition. The two Arab parties are projected to win as many as 17 seats — a remarkable show of strength that could make them Mr. Eisenkot’s only path to toppling Mr. Netanyahu.
On Wednesday, Mr. Eisenkot did not explicitly mention the Arab parties and instead pledged to build “a stable Zionist government.”
Most of the votes were expected to be counted by Wednesday, though the final tally could take days. Lengthy negotiations could follow as political parties try to assemble a governing majority. If those talks fail, the country could head to a second round of elections — a scenario that has played out before. For Mr. Netanyahu, running down the clock in the hope of securing a stronger showing in a fresh election could be his strongest shot at retaining his role as prime minister.
The uncertainty did not stop the leading candidates from making triumphant late-night speeches to their supporters.
Mr. Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief of staff, struck a defiant tone toward Mr. Netanyahu, saying: “Tonight we got the answer: The public opted for change.”
A few hours later, Mr. Netanyahu told supporters that his party, Likud, had emerged as the largest in Israel. “We must form a strong right-wing government,” he said.
Here’s what else we are covering:
Herzog’s role: President Isaac Herzog of Israel holds a largely ceremonial position, except after national elections, when it falls to him to select a potential prime minister. Read more ›
More votes: The exit polls do not reflect the hundreds of thousands of votes cast at special polling stations, including at military bases, hospitals, prisons and embassies. In Israel’s 2022 election, those votes tended to favor Mr. Netanyahu and his allies.
Regional implications: Israel’s neighbors in the Middle East had little hope that the election would fundamentally change Israel’s security doctrine, which has hardened since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023. Read more ›
Initial results: The 70 percent of the votes counted indicate that Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition will receive about 54 seats, Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc will get roughly 49, and the Arab parties will reach 17. But the numbers could still easily shift.
The initial results in the Israeli election released on Wednesday showed that there was no outright winner, and it may take weeks for it to become clear who will be able to form the next government.
But even if no government is formed, the Israeli Parliament will open on Nov. 10, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s opponents could be well-placed to take control of the legislative process.
The Parliament, or Knesset, will open with a swearing in of the 120 lawmakers. Both of the main blocs of Jewish parties likely fell short of winning a majority of seats, and both are reluctant to form a government that relies on a partnership with two predominantly Arab parties.
But even if the main anti-Netanyahu bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot , does not join with Arab parties to form a government, they remain united on some issues. If they join forces in parliamentary votes, they could stymie some of the Netanyahu government’s most contentious policies.
The first requirement would be to choose a new speaker of the house, so that the opposition could take control of the parliamentary agenda, key committees and start enacting laws, experts say.
“I’m not saying it’s a good scenario to take the Knesset and not be able to form the government,” said Gayil Talshir, a political scientist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem who is advising the opposition. “It’s a disaster. But this is the hand they are dealt, and they have to play it.”
One of the issues on which Mr. Eisenkot’s bloc and Arab parties agree — beyond wanting to unseat Mr. Netanyahu — is the need for an independent state inquiry into the government’s failure to prevent the Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.
Mr. Netanyahu, who has never taken responsibility for his government’s lapses in failing to stop the attack, has refused to allow such an inquiry. In the new Parliament, the opposition parties could work to establish one.
Another point that both sides agree on is a desire to overturn laws to carry out a sweeping overhaul of the judiciary .
Supporters of the Netanyahu government’s divisive plan said it was necessary to rein in what they saw as an overactive judiciary, to restore the balance between the branches of government and give more power to elected officials. Critics, however, said the proposed measures would remove checks on government power.
“Damaging legislation and damaging practices were introduced, but they can still be reversed,” said Yohanan Plesner, president of the Israel Democracy Institute, a nonpartisan research group.
Other contentious laws that could be challenged include one that politicized the process for appointing Supreme Court judges, and others that weakened the authority of the attorney general and expanded the authority of rabbinical courts.
Opposition members have also raised the idea of introducing legislation to bar a candidate charged with a crime from forming a government or to limit a prime minister to two terms in office.
Both of those efforts would be aimed at Mr. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest serving prime minister who is standing trial on corruption charges.
But such proposals would be problematic, experts say, because they could be seen as laws targeting Mr. Netanyahu personally and so would likely be challenged in Israel’s Supreme Court.
Such laws would also not apply retroactively, say, to a candidate who had been indicted in the past, Suzie Navot, an Israeli professor of constitutional law, said.
“They would not pass easily,” she said. She added the court could postpone such laws so that they could only come into effect in the next Knesset, or even strike them down.
David M. Halbfinger contributed reporting.
No party is expected to achieve a clear victory, which means the election will likely only be the first step in determining who will form the next government. Here’s how that might unfold.

A woman said she locked herself in a bathroom after realising her then-husband had allowed someone else in the bedroom while she was blindfolded and having sex, a jury has heard.
In a police interview played at Winchester Crown Court, Joanne Young said she was restrained when she felt a hand on her wrist which she believed did not belong to her now ex-husband Philip Young.
Joanne - who has waived her legal right to anonymity - said Young, who has admitted drugging and raping her, later apologised and told her he had invited someone to watch the couple have sex after browsing online forums.
Four men who Young is alleged to have recruited to abuse his wife at their home are now on trial.
Warning: This story contains distressing details
On the second day of the four men's trial, two police interviews with Joanne were played to the court.
During the first interview, dated 29 July 2024, Joanne said the incident when she hid in the bathroom had happened in February 2023 after a night out with friends.
She told police she could not "remember all of it", but said Young had come upstairs after she had gone to bed.
Joanne said she "woke up with a blindfold and restraints on" and loosened the restraint on her right hand and then the left. At that point, she said, she felt a hand grip her wrist.
She said Young - who she believed was at the end of the bed - said "get down" to someone as she tried to take her blindfold off.
Joanne said she then saw someone ducking at the end of the bed and she ran to the bathroom and locked the door.
"The bed is a really big bed. So to have someone on the end of the bed and the left was not possible… I knew immediately," she told police.
The jury heard the couple discussed the incident, with Joanne telling police it was the first time she had ever seen her then-husband cry.
Joanne said she asked Young if he had ever invited anyone to watch them have sex before, which he denied.
"It was so intrusive. I was so upset. He knows I would have never said yes to that," she told police.
Joanne told the officer: "I didn't know if I should stay in the relationship or get myself out of the situation."
She said she took the incident as a "one-off" and tried to "move on".
Asked by an officer if there was a discussion between Young and Joanne about having someone else in the relationship, she said: "There was a joke years ago, a bit of banter, where he said in the kitchen something like 'would you ever want to sleep with someone else?'.
"I said no, and he said 'as long as I can watch you'. We laughed it off but it was a no."
She added: "It was never a part of our relationship. There'd never been a discussion. He never asked me what I wanted, it wasn't a conversation."
On the day Young was arrested, Joanne said he admitted to her he had shared images of her online without her consent.
Joanne said it had felt like a "kick in the stomach" and she was left in "shock and utter confusion".
She said: "How he could do that to me. How he could do something that's so intimate that's not allowed. How can he do it? How can you do that and think that was OK?"
The prosecution also read out statements from people who had been friends with Joanne and Young during their marriage.
Joanne's friend Susan said she thought the couple had a "dream relationship" before Joanne told her about the alleged incident of February 2023.
"She was in a real dark place about what happened," the statement said.
"After telling me, life went back to normal but what I witnessed from Jo was she didn't seem herself and that Phil had crossed a line from what he had done.
"Jo explained she was torn about why would Phil do this to her. She was in shock and seemed to be numb."
Emma Brown, who the court was told had been best friends with the couple since 2009, said Young "could handle his drink" and she "never saw him noticeably drunk".
"He was always on his mobile phone... I didn't know what he was doing as I didn't look at it," she added.

Jurors were shown videos earlier which allegedly showed Sanderson-Doyle, Wilkins and Macksoni sexually assaulting Joanne.
Young, a former Conservative Swindon councillor, previously admitted 14 counts of voyeurism, 11 of rape, 11 of administering a substance with intent, seven of assault by penetration, four of sexual assault and one of publishing an obscene article.
He also published more than 500 intimate images and videos of his ex-wife and recorded her doing private acts for his own sexual gratification without her consent between 2010 and 2024.
A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street, Somerset, has admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.
Young and Hamilton will be sentenced at the end of the trial, which is expected to last up to four weeks.

Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. The company announced on Wednesday that users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”
The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across. The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined.
The company says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.
Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media, where algorithms play a significant role in shaping what users see.
With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.
Of course, not everyone will welcome the change, as some users may prefer the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined, rather than having recommended content mixed into their home feed. Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have already expressed their frustration with the change.
Reddit says users can switch between feeds and return to the one they last viewed the next time they open the platform.
It’s worth noting that although Reddit has long recommended posts from outside users’ subscribed communities, the new layout gives those recommendations their own feed on the homepage.
“This new feed experience is a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant – an idea, a connection, a unique perspective, or even a new interest,” the company wrote in a blog post . “A more human internet is not just something you sit back and watch, it is something you find value in and want to participate in.”
The new feed experience is rolling out globally over the next few weeks, the company says.

articles.title_orig: FDA scientists opposed the Trump administration’s effort to ease peptides access
articles.title_zh: FDA scientists opposed the Trump administration’s effort to ease peptides access
articles.content_orig:
The Department of Health and Human Services is giving compounding pharmacies a temporary green light to make six peptides while the agency continues to work on a formal rule change.
In a notice filed Wednesday, the agency said it would exercise “enforcement discretion,” meaning it will not take legal action against compounding pharmacies that make the six unapproved peptides. In practice, that means these pharmacies can start offering them now, even though the peptides aren’t yet on the Food and Drug Administration’s list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make.
The six peptides are BPC-157, epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, semax and TB-500.
They’ve been promoted online as treatments for everything from faster healing to younger-looking skin and a longer lifespan. None are approved by the FDA, and the agency’s own scientists concluded there is insufficient data to prove they are safe and effective.
The FDA said compounding pharmacies must certify the identity and purity of the compounds. They must also now report side effects, which was not previously mandated.
The move comes as a growing “gray market” has sprung up around peptides, where retailers sell them labeled “for research use only,” a legal workaround that lets them claim they aren’t meant for humans. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and others have argued that allowing peptides to be compounded would move people away from this gray market and toward safer products.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, HHS is working to put prevention and patient safety at the center of health care—and that includes confronting the risks of black-market peptides,” Emily Hilliard, an HHS spokesperson, said in a statement.
Dr. Peter Lurie, a former FDA official who now leads the Center for Science in the Public Interest watchdog group, said the FDA was essentially “turning a blind eye” to widen access to drugs that have not been proven to work.
Compounding pharmacies generally may use only ingredients the FDA has added to an official list known as the bulk drugs substances list. Adding an ingredient requires the FDA to propose a rule, take public comment and issue a final rule, a process that can take several months.
The agency took a step toward that process in July, when an FDA advisory panel narrowly voted in favor of adding six peptides to the bulk list. The panel included six new appointees with ties to the peptide industry and another who is the son of a U.S. representative who has pushed Kennedy to make peptides more available. (During that meeting, some committee members expressed concerns that the recommendation could make it harder for the FDA to say no to other unapproved drugs in the future.)
On Tuesday and Wednesday, the FDA was scheduled to meet outside groups, including Medivant Healthcare, a compounding pharmacy that offers peptides, according to Reginfo.gov , a federal website that tracks government regulations.
Shabbir Safdar, executive director of the Partnership for Safe Medicines, which researches the dangers of counterfeit medicines, said both the enforcement discretion and upcoming rule change would expose Americans to “untested dangerous substances.”
“Imagine what it means for the nation’s top drug regulator to announce they won’t enforce the laws on people making completely untested compounds and distributing them to the public,” Safdar said.
Berkeley Lovelace Jr. is a health and medical reporter for NBC News. He covers the Food and Drug Administration, with a special focus on Covid vaccines, prescription drug pricing and health care. He previously covered the biotech and pharmaceutical industry with CNBC.

Shares of Stellantis were up Wednesday as the European car giant's third-quarter results showed it was making progress with its 60 billion euro turnaround plan.
Third-quarter revenues rose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier.
The automaker's industrial free cash flow improved to negative 4 billion euros, up from negative 4.3 billion the year prior.
Stellantis on Wednesday also reconfirmed its 2026 guidance and target to achieve positive free cash flow next year, which is a main focus for investors.
"Q3 was soft, but consensus expectations were far lower. Key here is that '26 Guidance was maintained while other auto OEMs and suppliers are cutting on elevated costs," RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan said Wednesday in an investor note.
Stellantis stock rose roughly 9% Wednesday in Milan and was up by 12% in early trading in New York, but it remains sharply down since the beginning of the year.
Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa told investors Wednesday that the company is ahead of schedule on its turnaround plan, which was announced in May. He said Stellantis expects to exceed its previously announced cost-cutting efforts of 6 billion euros under the plan by 2028, including 2.4 billion euros to start 2027.
"We are very confident in reaffirming our '26 guidance. Those include '27 free cash flow positive," Filosa said Wednesday in response to concerns about the carmaker's ability to achieve its free cash flow target.
Stellantis' 2026 guidance includes a mid-single-digit percentage increase in net revenue and a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin.
Stellantis' turnaround plan includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products.
Stellantis is targeting roughly 23% revenue growth, from 154 billion euros last year to 190 billion euros by 2030, with a 7% adjusted operating margin by then.
European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition.
Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it would reduce its exposure to China as car sales decline in the region. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz said its third-quarter car sales slumped due to a "challenging market environment," in the country.
Earlier this month, Filosa told CNBC that European regulators need to do more to incentivize carmakers to manufacture vehicles in the region to fend off Chinese rivals.
Filosa called for regulation that "incentivizes, rewards, and protects the ones that are able to demonstrate that they design cars, engineer cars."

US military says the restrictions on the electric vehicles at Kadena airbase also apply to delivery drivers and taxis
One of America’s biggest overseas military bases has banned vehicles made by the Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD over security concerns, the US military in Japan said on Tuesday.
The ban, which went into effect this week at Kadena airbase on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa , has fueled speculation that similar measures could be taken at other US military facilities as part of Washington’s crackdown on Chinese technology it suspects of being used to collect sensitive information.
“These vehicles present an unacceptable and unmitigable risk to our personnel and our mission,” Lieut Col Alli Stormer, a spokesperson for the US air force 18th Wing at Kadena, said in a statement.
The restrictions apply to all BYD vehicles, including privately owned cars, taxis and delivery vehicles, reports said, adding that security personnel stationed at the base’s gates had been instructed to block BYD vehicles and instruct drivers to turn around.
Kadena, the biggest US air force base east Asia, would be directly involved in responding to a crisis involving China , Russia or North Korea .
Its inventory includes the powerful Typhon missile system, which is said to be capable of firing Tomahawk missiles as far as 1,600km, putting parts of China and Russia within striking distance. Kadena also hosts fighter planes and aircraft used for mid-air refuelling, surveillance and reconnaissance, according to its website.
The move comes amid concerns of potential information leaks via vehicle-mounted technologies such as cameras, sensors and GPS devices, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency said.
American military officials have not identified a specific threat, but the ban is part of wider measures taken by the US and other western countries to restrict Chinese smart technology in vehicles, mobile phones and other devices they fear could be used to “spy” on their owners.
In June the Pentagon added BYD to a list of 188 Chinese firms it believes have ties to the country’s military, drawing a protest from Beijing. The blacklist also includes the automaker Nio, e-commerce firm Alibaba and internet company Baidu.
The US defence department banned the sale and use of smartphones from Chinese companies Huawei and ZTE at military bases worldwide in 2018, again citing security concerns.
China has imposed similar restrictions on US-made Tesla vehicles. In 2021, it barred them from some government compounds due to security concerns over ⁠cameras installed on the vehicles. Beijing removed that restriction in 2024 after Tesla won an endorsement from the country’s top auto industry association.
BYD, which has not immediately responded publicly to the Kadena ban, overtook Tesla as the world’s biggest seller of battery-electric vehicles in 2025.
It is now expanding overseas, including in the world’s fourth-biggest auto market, Japan , where in July it launched its Racco electric minicar in the hope that the small, cost-efficient vehicle would carve out a place in a market dominated by domestic brands.

articles.content_orig:
Ethiopia has received 12 Russian-made Su-35 fighter jets and announced a deal involving four S-400 air defence system batteries, strengthening its military capabilities as renewed fighting in the country raises security concerns.
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the aircraft delivery during a visit to Moscow, where he attended a Russia-Africa summit and met Russian President Vladimir Putin .
“I would like to express my gratitude to my friend, Russian President Vladimir Putin, for his dedication in ensuring we received these warplanes a year ahead of our agreed schedule,” he said on his X account.
The Ethiopian leader did not disclose the value of the arms agreement, when the S-400 air defence systems would be delivered or where the aircraft and batteries would be deployed.
The acquisition comes as Ethiopia faces mounting security challenges, particularly in the northern Tigray region. A rebel alliance launched an offensive last month, raising fears of a renewed conflict following the war between 2020 and 2022 that killed hundreds of thousands of people.
During the previous conflict, Ethiopia relied heavily on foreign-made drones to strengthen its air power and turn the tide of fighting.
The latest escalation has also deepened tensions with neighbouring Eritrea, which Addis Ababa accuses of supporting the rebels. Asmara has denied the allegations.
Ethiopia’s reported acquisition highlights Russia ’s continued efforts to deepen defence partnerships across Africa, where several countries rely on Russian aircraft and military equipment.
Sudan ’s Defence Ministry is reportedly negotiating with Moscow to acquire Su-30 and Su-35 fighter jets in exchange for allowing Russia to establish a major naval facility on the Red Sea, according to Military Watch Magazine.
Algeria , meanwhile, received a batch of Russian Su-34M strike fighters in May, adding to its substantial fleet of Russian-made military aircraft.
Earlier reports from Algerian defence publications indicated that the country had ordered 14 Su-34ME strike fighters, 14 Su-35E fighter jets and 14 Su-57E fifth-generation aircraft.
These deals underscore Russia’s continuing role in Africa’s defence procurement market, even as Moscow faces pressure on its military production and export capacity amid the war in Ukraine.

articles.title_zh: Italian judge frees protest suspect, prompting Meloni fury
articles.content_orig:
Youssef Siher exercised his right to remain silent when questioned by preliminary investigations judge Tiziana Landoni in Milan’s San Vittore prison on Tuesday.
Investigations into the unrest that rocked the centre of the Lombard capital on 17 and 18 October are proceeding on two separate tracks: messages found by investigators in a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members, and the Milan prosecutor’s inquiry into Siher’s alleged role in organising and spreading content linked to the so-called 17 October Movement.
The Monza and Brianza Digos (General Investigations and Special Operations Division) began investigating after finding a message in a chat in which a user urged others not to put their balaclavas on straight away, to avoid being identified by police.
On 22 October, acting on a warrant from the Milan juvenile prosecutor’s office, investigators searched the home of the teenager believed to have written the message. They found a balaclava and an Under Armour T-shirt thought to have been stolen from a shop looted in Milan. A search of another minor turned up a second T-shirt of the same brand, also believed to have been taken during the looting.
But it was the first boy’s mobile phone that gave investigators their most significant lead, pointing them to a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members. The conversations referred to weapons, knives, smoke bombs and firecrackers, as well as plans to attack officers, snatch their weapons, damage police vehicles and set public buildings on fire.
Messages cited by investigators include “And we steal their weapons”, “Let’s grab one, beat him up and take his weapon” and “Hey guys, if we’re going to protest, let’s set fire to a government building”. Others urged people to get hold of knives, clubs and pepper spray, while some discussed stealing cars and targeting businesses, with references to a “Gucci robbery” and a McDonald’s.
The chats also mentioned further demonstrations planned for 24 October, which risked turning violent. The information gathered helped trigger a nationwide preventive operation.
On 24 October, around 150 personal and home searches were carried out in several Italian provinces, coordinated by the Central Directorate of Preventive Police and involving Digos units and Flying Squads from various cities. The main aim was to find illegally held weapons and ammunition.
In Brianza, the checks covered 32 people living in 16 municipalities, including Monza, Seregno, Giussano, Carate Brianza, Limbiate, Nova Milanese and Desio.
Officers seized folding and butterfly knives, a hatchet with “1312” engraved on its blade – a numerical code for the acronym ACAB (“All Cops Are B*****ds”) – knuckledusters, a telescopic baton, two blank-firing pistols missing their red safety caps, glass breakers, balaclavas and other items classed as offensive weapons.
Investigators are continuing to piece together the alleged conduct and identify anyone else responsible.
Siher was detained on 24 October and is accused of incitement to commit crimes, aggravated by terrorist intent, and of organised violence during public demonstrations. Prosecutors say he runs the social media channels of the 17 October Movement, which was set up after the clashes in central Milan.
Landoni must now decide whether to validate his detention and grant the request for him to be held in prison pending trial, submitted by chief prosecutor Marcello Viola and prosecutor Francesca Crupi, who attended the hearing. Prosecutors argue there is a risk he could flee or reoffend. A decision is expected by 28 October.
Siher is represented by lawyers Benedetto Ciccarone and Yasmina Abu Sharar, who deny he incited violence or terrorism and have asked for his release.

Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management on Wednesday made an offer to buy Wendy's for roughly $1.4 billion in a move that would make the fast-food chain a privately held company.
Trian has been a long-term shareholder in Wendy's and Peltz's hedge fund is leading a group that offered to buy the struggling fast food giant at a price of $7.35 a share in cash.
The $1.4 billion bid to purchase Wendy's is about a 20% premium over the company's valuation of $1.2 billion at Tuesday's market close.
The offer by the Trian-led group was confirmed by FOX Business and disclosed in a filing on Wednesday. The Wall Street Journal first reported on the offer.
WENDY'S LOSES STATUS AS SECOND-LARGEST BURGER CHAIN AFTER 6-YEAR RUN
Wendy's stock has struggled over the last five years. (Mike Campbell/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Wendy's shares have fallen about 68% over the last five years as of Wednesday's market open, though the stock surged nearly 17% on Wednesday morning following the news.
The Trian-led group bidding to buy Wendy's includes restaurant operator Flynn Group along with investment firms BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners.
The group said in a letter that making Wendy's a private company would better allow it to carry out a complicated turnaround process that's expected to take multiple years and entail major capital investment .
MAJOR WENDY'S FRANCHISEE FILES FOR BANKRUPTCY
Nelson Peltz, founder and CEO of Trian Fund Management, said in the letter that Wendy's would be better positioned as a private company. (Marco Bello/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"Wendy's sits at a critical juncture. The external environment has become increasingly challenging given the significant pressures on the U.S. consumer , economic uncertainty, persistent commodity inflation and intensifying competition, particularly with the QSR burger category," the group wrote.
"The business requires significant capital investment to de-lever and execute the strategic initiatives needed to turn system performance around," it added.
WENDY'S TO CLOSE HUNDREDS OF RESTAURANTS AS COMPANY LOOKS TO FOCUS ON VALUE TO BOOST SALES
The letter said that in the group's view, the alternative to accepting the offer to take Wendy's private is "continued exposure to market volatility while the Company works to manage its balance sheet against approaching debt maturities and the significant capital investment needed for the brand, all under the short-term pressure of public markets ."
"We believe private ownership is the better path and provides the patient, long-duration capital needed to restore the business and the franchise system to a position of strength," the group added.
